title: SO Emission in the Dynamically Perturbed Protoplanetary Disks around CQ Tau and MWC 758
question: Is SO emission in the spiral-hosting, dynamically perturbed disks of CQ Tau and MWC 758 detected, where does it arise, and is it linked to dynamical perturbations?

recipe.goal: Self-calibrate archival EBs and build continuum-subtracted datasets
recipe.method: Pseudo-continuum from line-flagged data, per-EB phase-only self-cal, EB alignment, iterative phase-only self-cal (short then combined baselines), amplitude rescaling, two amplitude+phase cycles, apply to full data, bin 30 s, uvcontsub
key_parameters: Pseudo-continuum made by flagging +/-15 km/s around 12CO, 13CO, C18O, DCN, SO, H2CO lines
Imaging of pseudo-continuum: multiscale, briggs robust=0.5, smallscalebias=0.6, cycleniter=300, gain=0.3
First phase-only round: infinite solint, antennas with <3 baselines and SNR<4 rejected
Amplitude+phase cycles: infinite solint, SNR<5 solutions flagged, amplitude gains >20% flagged

recipe.method: tclean multiscale continuum imaging from the final self-calibrated, 30 s-averaged data
tclean cube imaging of continuum-subtracted data, multiscale, natural weighting with uv-taper, Keplerian or continuum mask
key_parameters: CQ Tau: 23 channels of 0.7 km/s; MWC 758: 7 channels of 1.4 km/s
natural weighting with Gaussian uv-taper 0.05 arcsec (CQ Tau) and 0.25 arcsec (MWC 758)

recipe.goal: Detect SO and measure line fluxes by shift-and-stack
recipe.method: gofish extraction of spectra from circular apertures, shifted to a common line centre assuming Keplerian rotation, stacked, and integrated
key_parameters: Aperture radius set where the cumulative SO emission flattens: 0.33 arcsec (CQ Tau), 0.80 arcsec (MWC 758)
Cubes over >200 km/s velocity range to estimate background noise in line-free channels
assumptions: Keplerian velocity field used to shift spectra

recipe.method: bettermoments integrated intensity, peak intensity and velocity maps without channel or threshold clipping
key_parameters: No channel or noise clipping applied

recipe.goal: Convert literature SO fluxes to a common 6_5-5_4 flux at 140 pc
recipe.method: LTE optically thin flux ratio (T = 30, 50, 70 K) and optically thick Rayleigh-Jeans ratio
key_parameters: Rescale fluxes to a common distance of 140 pc
assumptions: Optically thick case: same excitation temperature and emitting area for both transitions

recipe.goal: Test correlations of SO flux with stellar and disk properties
recipe.method: Pearson correlation coefficient and p-values between SO flux and stellar/disk parameters
